newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel stable against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel stable against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was fixed almost unchanged against the dollar and the basket of key foreign currecnies on Thursday in dull trading, dealers said.
"Trading continues to be very quiet and trendless. The shekel rose slightly against the dollar after the U.S. currecny declined in Europe," said Ilan Zadka of United Mizrahi Bank.
"The Bank of Israel was the main player in the market as it had to intervene in local trading to buy dollars to support the basket," Zadka said.
Traders estimated that the central bank bought under $100 million to keep the basket rate from falling below its trading band.

The shekel is allowed to fluctuate in a band of seven percent above or below a sloping mid-point designed to devalue the Israeli currency at a rate of six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3510 shekels against 3.3520 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6386 shekels against 3.6384 on Wednesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7115 shekels per 100 yen against 2.7058 on Wednesday and against the mark at 1.9851 shekels against 1.9806 on Wednesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.3500 shekels.
